Plot the sensitivity analysis of the SROC curves

Source: R/plot.srocsa.R
plot.srocsa.Rd

Plot method for 'srocsa' objects. This function plots the SROC curves and the summary points for each marginal selection probability \(p\), from the sensitivity analysis by srocsa.t or tsrocsa.lrt. For srocsa.t, one plot is created. For tsrocsa.lrt, one plot is created at each time point, with the title time = xx; in an interactive session the user is prompted ("Hit <Return> to see next plot") before each new time point. The same \(p\) has the same color and line type at all the time points. Alternatively, all the time points can be overlaid in one panel (overlay = TRUE): the color indicates the time point and the line type indicates \(p\).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'srocsa'
plot(
  x,
  time = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  overlay = FALSE,
  ask = NULL,
  sroc.cols = NULL,
  sroc.lty = 1,
  sroc.lwd = 2,
  add.spoint = TRUE,
  sp.pch = 19,
  sp.cex = 1.2,
  plot.ci = FALSE,
  spoint.region = FALSE,
  ci.level = 0.95,
  ci.lty = 2,
  ci.lwd = 1,
  add.study = FALSE,
  study.size = c("fixed", "precision"),
  study.pch = 1,
  study.cex = 1,
  study.col = NULL,
  add.sauc = TRUE,
  legend.pos = "bottomright",
  legend.cex = 0.85,
  main = NULL,
  xlab = "FPR (1 - specificity)",
  ylab = "TPR (sensitivity)",
  n.grid = 300,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted object returned by the function srocsa.t or tsrocsa.lrt.

time

Time points to plot (only for the results from tsrocsa.lrt). If time = NULL (default), all the time points are plotted.

p

Values of the marginal selection probability \(p\) to plot. If p = NULL (default), all the values are plotted.

overlay

Logical; if TRUE, all the selected time points of tsrocsa.lrt are drawn in one panel (ignored for srocsa.t, which has one panel).

ask

Logical; whether to wait for <Return> before each new time point. Default NULL means TRUE when more than one plot is drawn on an interactive device.

sroc.cols

Colors of the SROC curves: one for each \(p\), or one for each time point when overlay = TRUE. Default uses grey colors (black for the first \(p\)), and hcl.colors (palette "Dark 3") for the time points when overlay = TRUE.

sroc.lty

Line types of the SROC curves, recycled over \(p\). When overlay = TRUE and it is not specified, 1, 2, 3, ... are used for the values of \(p\).

sroc.lwd

Line width of the SROC curves.

add.spoint

Whether to add the summary points on the SROC curves.

sp.pch

Type of the summary points.

sp.cex

Size of the summary points.

plot.ci

Whether to add the pointwise confidence bands of the SROC curves (delta method using var.ml).

spoint.region

Whether to add the confidence regions of the summary points.

ci.level

Confidence level of the bands and regions. Default 0.95.

ci.lty, ci.lwd

Line type and width of the bands and regions.

add.study

Whether to add the observed (published) studies (\((1 - \mathrm{spec}_i, \mathrm{sens}_i)\), after continuity correction), stored in the attribute "data" of x.

study.size

Size of the study points: "fixed" (default) or "precision", proportional to \(1/\sqrt{v_1 + v_2}\) relative to its mean.

study.pch, study.cex

Symbol and (base) size of the study points.

study.col

Color of the study points. Default NULL uses grey, or the (semi-transparent) color of each time point when overlay = TRUE.

add.sauc

Whether to show the SAUC (and its CI) for each \(p\) in the legend.

legend.pos

Position of the legend. See legend. NULL suppresses the legend.

legend.cex

Size of the legend text.

main

Title of the plot. If main = NULL (default), time = xx is used for the time-dependent results ("Time-dependent SROC curves" when overlay = TRUE), and no title for the results from srocsa.t.

xlab

Label of x-axis.

ylab

Label of y-axis.

n.grid

Number of grid points to draw each curve.

...

Other arguments in function plot.default.

Value

x, invisibly. Called for the side effect of plotting.

Details

For \(p < 1\) in tsrocsa.lrt, the SROC curve is calculated from \((\mu_1, \mu_2, \tau_1, \tau_2, \rho_1)\) of the trivariate model, i.e., the parameters of the logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity.

See also

srocsa.t, tsrocsa.lrt, plot.sroc

Examples

## load data
data(IVD)

fit1 <- srocsa.t(TP = TP, FN = FN, TN = TN, FP = FP, data = IVD, sa.p = c(1, 0.8, 0.6))
plot(fit1)


## set the colors and add the studies
plot(fit1, sroc.cols = c("black", "blue", "red"), add.study = TRUE)


## only p = 1 and p = 0.6, with confidence bands
plot(fit1, p = c(1, 0.6), plot.ci = TRUE, sroc.cols = c("black", "red"))


# \donttest{
## time-dependent results (see ?tsrocsa.lrt for fit2)
## plot(fit2)                           # one plot per time point; press <Return> for the next
## plot(fit2, time = 60)                # one time point
## plot(fit2, overlay = TRUE)           # all time points in one panel (color: time, line type: p)
## plot(fit2, overlay = TRUE, p = 0.8)  # all time points for one p
# }
